48.original: Thank you again, but I shall manage on my own.

49.original: Forgive me, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>, but I cannot in good conscience ignore the callous disregard that woman showed for her kinsman!

50.original: We must seek her out at once! With me!

51.original: Such contempt as was in their eyes I have never known... But for the soul to live on as they say is not something I can so easily accept.

52.original: Do they truly believe this? All of them? That in death there can be rebirth? ...Retribution?

53.original: ...In any event, we came here in search of information. We cannot leave without speaking with her people.

54.original: Err...that is to say, then, that death is essentially meaningless?

55.original: I know you! Reunion! The travelers with the Mol girl!

56.original: I marked you after I left the Oronir. Ones from Doma, others I could not place.

57.original: My name is Koko. Welcome to Dotharl Khaa.

58.original: Hm? Koko sounds to your ear the name of a woman? Well, of course. That would be because it is.

59.original: I died a woman and was reborn a man. It is of no moment─the soul is the soul, and the flesh the flesh.

60.original: Perhaps you scoff? Many would. Many look only to the name and the flesh, and let these things dictate their perceptions.

61.original: Consider Sadu Khatun. Three times before she died a man, yet she returns as a woman the fourth. Yet she is no less fierce, and any outsider foolish enough to think so will learn the truth to their peril.

62.original: Is the khatun woman or man? A stupid question. She is Sadu.

63.original: The cycle of death and rebirth? It is simply that. Take me─I died in battle with the Hotgo. Fiercely did I fight, and so I returned.

64.original: Alas, we know naught of our past lives. I must learn what it means to be Qoyar again and again. It is difficult to remember everything, but important.

65.original: It filled me with such excitement when they first told me of my deeds, as did my friends!

66.original: Impressive, is it not? 'Twas slain by my boy.

67.original: We were childhood friends, he and I, before he fell and returned. A master of the bow. It is good to see that he retains his skill.

68.original: We competed against one another in the hunts. Though I knew he would return, I never expected it to be as my son!

69.original: Ah, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>. You have completed your inquiries?

70.original: Aye, it is as she said. They believe with every fiber of their being that their bravest warriors will be reborn.

71.original: As for me, I observed some of their warriors at practice. They are as formidable as the Oronir, perhaps more, and their weapons are their equal as well.

72.original: Yet while they do not lack in skill and resources, 'tis plain to see that their numbers are inferior...
